page: Microsoft Azure B2ats_v2 is a burstable virtual machine instance built on the x86_64 architecture. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz, the instance provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyperthreading. Hardware cache resources include 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Cryptographic and bit-manipulation extensions such as AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and AVX are available, while AVX-512 and matrix extensions are absent. The instance does not include a dedicated GPU accelerator or local instance storage, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The memory subsystem features 1.0 GB of total RAM, yielding an allocation of 0.5 GB per vCPU. This low memory footprint restricts data caching and concurrent process headroom, as evidenced by a cached small-block read memory bandwidth of 140.76 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score categorized in the bottom 10 percent. Single-core stress-ng tests reached 2701.19, ranking in the top 25 percent due to the high peak core clock frequency. However, multi-core stress-ng performance scored the same value, reflecting aggregate throughput limitations typical of burstable fractional allocations and narrow physical core counts.

Additional synthetic tests demonstrate the baseline constraints of the resource profile. PassMark CPU encryption scored 2150.03, physics scored 391.83, and overall CPU scored 3130.58, placing overall compute capacity in the lower tiers. In application metrics, Redis SET operations achieved 2.25 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 2.77 GB per second. Because CPU cycles operate on a burstable credit model and RAM is constrained to 1.0 GB, sustained heavy execution will throttle performance. The B2ats_v2 is suitable for lightweight background utilities, small development test environments, low-traffic web proxies, or intermittent tasks where cost-effective entry-level compute is prioritized over memory capacity and sustained throughput.
description: Microsoft Azure B2ats_v2 is an entry-level burstable virtual machine equipped with 2 vCPUs from a single physical core on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at 3.525 GHz. Configured with 1.0 GB of RAM, the instance features a 0.5 GB per vCPU ratio, x86_64 architecture, and standard instruction extensions including AES and AVX, but lacks dedicated GPU hardware and local storage. Benchmark results show strong single-core stress-ng performance at 2701.19, but multi-core throughput, PassMark CPU at 3130.58, and PassMark memory remain in lower percentiles due to core and memory limitations. Application testing recorded 2.25 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.77 GB per second of static web serving throughput. Designed for cost-efficient minimal footprints, the B2ats_v2 fits low-traffic microservices, basic testing environments, and periodic lightweight background tasks that do not require sustained compute or substantial memory buffers.
